Official Explanations.what_happened: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites. Today, we're announcing our plans to support a shared AI training…

sources.name: Google Search Central Blog
sources.excerpt: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites. Today, we're announcing our plans to support a shared AI training control in robots.txt. This will help websites express their AI training preferences across multiple AI providers in a single step and is based on work from the AIPREF working group at the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). This builds on our long history of providing website owners with clear controls, including through Google-Extended, the AI training control we've offered since 2023.
sources.author: Google Search Central Blog

sources.name: glenngabe
sources.excerpt: I published a three-part series on Reddit's AI translations documenting the rise and fall of that content. Those translations (tens of millions of urls across many countries) took a big hit with the May 2026 core update and June spam update. Now Reddit is explaining more about that drop. So DO NOT just translate any content via AI. Make sure it's high quality. If not, you can get hammered. Reddit: "Our machine-translated content (AI-translated content) is being ranked lower, which affects our international traffic.
